name: Disco-X
intro: DiscoX是一个针对专家领域语篇级翻译的新基准，旨在解决现有评估方法主要关注片段级准确性和流畅性的不足。它包含200篇来自7个领域的专业文本，平均长度超过1700个词元。同时，该基准还开发了Metric-S，一个无参考的自动评估系统，用于评估翻译的准确性、流畅性和适当性。实验表明，即使是最先进的LLM在这些任务上的表现仍落后于人类专家，验证了DiscoX的难度。
build_method: 领域专家策展, 语言专家同行评审, 双模型难度过滤, 专家评分点标注
metric: Metric-S = Accuracy + Fluency + Appropriateness（上限 60/20/20；分量下限 0）
eval_feature: 指令失败归零, 准确性/流畅性/适切性三裁判, 根因去重, 精确扣分, 主协议与 2025-12 发布分支分离
scale: 665个候选 → 200个任务, 英译中100 + 中译英100, 7个领域, 平均1712.17词元
build_method_en: Domain-expert curation, linguistic peer review, two-model difficulty filtering, expert rubric annotation
eval_feature_en: Instruction-failure Zero Gate, Three Metric-S Judges, Root-cause Deduplication, Exact Deductions, Main-vs-Dec-2025 Protocol Boundary
intro_en: DiscoX is a new benchmark for expert-domain discourse-level translation, designed to address the limitations of existing evaluations that mainly focus on segment-level accuracy and fluency. It includes 200 professional texts from 7 domains, with an average length of over 1700 tokens. The benchmark also introduces Metric-S, a reference-free automatic evaluation system for assessing translation accuracy, fluency, and appropriateness. Experiments show that even state-of-the-art LLMs still lag behind human experts on these tasks, confirming the difficulty of DiscoX.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2511.10984v2 / OpenReview OTCfZ6h8Pe, §§2.1–3.4, Figures 3–4, official repository ByteDance-Seed/DiscoX@fab17983fceb169f561b5bcce422e1a62cc24196, and Hugging Face dataset ByteDance-Seed/DiscoX@f6d3d51d0c37ed9052ff65e78bf6cd55b815c2aa. The pinned release contains 200 tasks (100 EN→ZH, 100 ZH→EN; 121 academic, 79 non-academic; seven fields). Construction uses 115 domain experts plus 18 linguistic specialists over 1,330 person-hours, texts of at least 1,500 Chinese characters or English words, four rubric categories averaging 9.38 checkpoints, a 665-task pool, linguistic peer review, and a gate where both SOTA models fail at least eight rubrics before final expert repair and selection. Metric-S first assigns zero to non-translation, continuation, or summary output. Valid translations go to accuracy, fluency, and appropriateness judges, then hierarchical causal-root deduplication: Extremely Critical Accuracy errors have the highest priority, expert checkpoint/rubric duplicates are second, and remaining overlaps are assigned to the causal root. Components are individually floored at zero: Accuracy starts at 60 with −5 expert-rubric/ordinary-major, −10 critical, and −50 extremely critical deductions; Fluency starts at 20 with −2 per issue; Appropriateness starts at 20 with −5 per issue. The main paper uses a simple translation prompt with Gemini-2.5-Pro; the December 2025 detailed-prompt release uses Gemini-3-Pro, so scores are not directly comparable across those settings. Paper validation samples 50 cases and reports 70.3% expert pairwise consistency; three repeated trials are stability analysis, not a mandatory score aggregation rule.
